T3. Long-term development [YES] — systemic lobbying conflicts and climate superfund legislation trajectory

Synopsis:
A new analysis by F Minus and Make Polluters Pay exposes a structural conflict of interest: the same congressional lobbying firms representing major fossil fuel companies (ExxonMobil, API, ConocoPhillips) are simultaneously lobbying on behalf of 300+ local governments seeking climate damage funding. Firms like Greenberg Traurig epitomize the contradiction — blocking state climate superfund laws for fossil fuel clients while securing climate resilience funding for municipalities. Fossil fuel industry lobbyists are shown to dominate opposition to superfund bills using debunked economic claims, while federal legislation (Stop Climate Shakedowns Act, Cruz/Hageman) seeks to nullify climate accountability lawsuits entirely.
